entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Phaedrus was an Epicurean philosopher. He was the head (scholarch) of the Epicurean school in Athens after the death of Zeno of Sidon around 75 BC, until his own death in 70 or 69 BC. He was a contemporary of Cicero, who became acquainted with him in his youth at Rome. During his residence in Athens Cicero renewed his acquaintance with him. Phaedrus was at that time an old man, and was already a leading figure of the Epicurean school. He was also on terms of friendship with Velleius, whom Cicero introduces as the defender of the Epicurean tenets in the De Natura Deorum, and especially with Atticus.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Phaedrus was a leading figure of the Epicurean school in Athens during Cicero's youth and adulthood, influencing the development of Epicureanism and its tenets. His friendship with prominent figures like Velleius and Atticus highlights his significance within the intellectual circles of ancient Rome.
